result.rationale: In db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb, `execute("SELECT ... WHERE s.name = 'embed_category'")[0]['id'].to_i` unconditionally dereferences the first row. Site settings only persist rows whose values differ from defaults, so on a fresh install (or a site that never set embed_category) the query returns zero rows and `[0]` is nil, raising NoMethodError and aborting db:migrate. The `if category_id == 0` fallback never runs because the crash happens first. Note the embeddable_hosts lookup just below is guarded with `cmd_tuples > 0`, showing the author knew rows could be missing bu

adjudication.rationale: In `db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb`, the migration does `execute(...)[0]['id'].to_i` on the result of a `SELECT ... WHERE s.name = 'embed_category'`. If that query returns zero rows, `[0]` is `nil` and `['id']` will raise `NoMethodError` before the later `if category_id == 0` fallback can run. The diff shows no guard (e.g., checking `cmd_tuples` or presence) for this first query, so the migration can crash on installs where there is no matching `site_settings` row / join result.
